query_preparation.promotion_rule: Official map/API/register/download capability may be VERIFIED or PREPARED_QUERY, but exact candidate result remains PENDING_RAW_RESPONSE until candidate-specific spatial/asset/address/record evidence and provenance are captured.

batches.c: Round 4 strategic road-noise mapping is modelled annual-average exposure based on 2021 inputs. Exact candidate-grid/geometry binding is required; it is not a measured façade level.
Different strategic-noise metrics describe different time periods and effects. Metric identity must be retained; one metric cannot be substituted for another.
Round 4 mapping also covers rail noise. Exact candidate intersection and source class are required before any rail-noise context is promoted.
The 2022 Round 4 maps are a snapshot derived from 2021 conditions. Later road, rail or building changes are not automatically reflected.
Strategic maps support prioritisation and action planning. An Important Area or action-plan context is not a site-specific mitigation requirement without exact designation evidence.
Strategic mapping is screening evidence and cannot replace a proposal-specific acoustic survey, façade assessment or plant-noise assessment.
AURN provides high-resolution automatic monitoring. Exact monitor identity, distance, site type and pollutant are required before relating readings to a candidate.
Near-real-time AURN values can be provisional; verified data follow QA/QC. Candidate evidence must preserve verification status and retrieval period.
The UK-AIR local dashboard exposes AQMA information. Exact candidate-to-AQMA relation is required; borough-wide presence does not prove parcel membership.
London borough diffusion tubes provide local NO2 monitoring but are methodologically different from reference monitors. Exact tube/site/year binding is required.
LAEI 2022 is the latest London emissions inventory found and received May 2026 revisions. Modelled emissions/concentrations are context, not exact measured parcel values.
Reference analysers, diffusion tubes and lower-cost sensors have different quality characteristics. Data types must not be merged as if directly equivalent.

batches.t: Groundwater Source Protection Zone exact-polygon gate
batches.c: EA Source Protection Zones are screening polygons around potable abstractions. Exact candidate polygon intersection and zone number are required.
Groundwater Safeguard Zones identify areas where additional pollution-control measures may be needed. Exact spatial binding is required.
EA water-resource zones describe water-company supply operating boundaries. Candidate-to-zone binding informs supply context but not connection capacity.
The EA real-time API exposes warning/alert areas and live states. Exact warning-area relation must be separated from long-term flood probability.
A current absence of a flood warning is not proof of no flood risk; warning services and long-term planning risk are different evidence types.
A water-resource-zone boundary identifies operational geography only. It does not establish developer connection capacity, pressure or reinforcement need.
UKPN Open Data exposes network assets and capacity-related datasets. Exact network asset/substation relation is required before candidate connection context.
Network headroom data can support early connection screening. Headroom is time- and network-state dependent and is not a connection offer.
Generation capacity and demand capacity are distinct. Candidate requirements must use the correct direction and voltage/network level.
UKPN NDP provides forward-looking headroom under scenarios. Scenario values are planning evidence, not guaranteed future available capacity.
DFES 2026 publishes LSOA-level low-carbon technology and demand scenarios. These are scenarios to 2050, not parcel forecasts.
DNOA identifies future capacity needs and preferred options. Proposed reinforcement or flexibility is not treated as delivered network capacity.
DfT open data provides record-level reported personal-injury collisions. Exact spatial/time filtering is required; proximity does not establish site causation.
2025 collision data are provisional pending final validation. Provisional records must be labelled and not silently mixed with final annual data.
2024 is the latest final validated full-year open dataset identified. It can provide a stable baseline but remains historical road-safety context.
Collision severity and STATS19 reporting/method changes must be preserved. Raw counts without exposure and road context are not a site safety score.
A candidate trend requires consistent spatial radius, years and reporting definitions. A single incident or year is not a robust trend.
GLA/Data.gov metadata may be republished or harvested; DfT record-level releases remain the canonical collision source for current detailed analysis.
Enfield maintains contaminated-land records and offers searches. Exact property/land search evidence is required; borough records do not imply candidate contamination.
Enfield states the whole borough is a smoke control area. This is borough-wide regulatory context, not evidence of candidate air quality or planning refusal.
Enfield as LLFA requires drainage strategy information for planning. Exact scheme layout, runoff and infiltration evidence are required before feasibility conclusions.
Flood-risk assessment requirements depend on site risk and proposal. Exact candidate risk sources must be resolved; generic borough flood context is insufficient.
Enfield requires Highway Safety Impact Assessment information for specified minor development types. Applicability depends on exact proposal type and access.
New flood-alleviation funding identifies planned schemes, but nearby future works are not treated as delivered protection or candidate benefit without exact status/location.
Havering publishes an Air Quality Annual Status Report 2025 for 2024. Monitoring-year and report-year must remain distinct.
Havering maintains the Part 2A public register. Exact site/register entry is required before any determined-contaminated-land conclusion.

batches.t: Havering property Land Quality Report gate
batches.c: Council Land Quality Reports can include historic uses and nearby environmental records. A commissioned property-specific report is stronger than borough-level screening.

batches.t: Havering Launders Lane determination isolation gate
batches.c: Arnold's Field/Launders Lane was formally determined contaminated land in 2025. That specific determination must never be generalized to unrelated Havering candidates.
Havering flood guidance distinguishes council, EA and water-company responsibilities. Exact flood/drainage source and responsible network must be identified.
Emergency flood advice describes response pathways, not long-term planning flood probability. Current incidents and strategic risk must remain separate.

batches.t: Lambeth Air Quality Action Plan current-status gate
batches.c: Lambeth's strategy index lists an Air Quality Action Plan 2026-2028 while older pages still expose 2023-25 material. Current plan/version must be resolved before use.
Lambeth uses diffusion tubes and automatic monitoring stations. Exact monitor identity, pollutant, period and method are required for candidate context.
Lambeth can carry out contaminated-land searches. Exact land/property search evidence is required before promoting contamination status.
Lambeth publishes environmental-permitting register resources in its air-quality archive. Exact regulated process/site relation is required.
The Soak up Lambeth programme identifies SuDS schemes across streets, parks, estates and schools. Nearby programme activity is not automatic site flood protection.
Lambeth's planning evidence includes older SFRA/surface-water documents. Historic evidence must be crosschecked against current EA/LLFA information before site use.
